title.zh: 卷25 列傳第17 李賢 弟遠
title.en: Volume 25 Biographies 17: Li Xian; brother Yuan
title.raw: 卷25 列傳第17 李賢 弟遠 Volume 25 Biographies 17: Li Xian; brother Yuan

sentences.zh: 李賢 弟遠

translations.literal: Li Xian; brother Yuan
translations.idiomatic: Li Xian; Li Yuan (younger brother)

sentences.zh: 李賢字賢和，其先隴西成紀人也。

translations.literal: Li Xian, styled Xianhe, his ancestors were men of Chengji in Longxi.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xian, styled Xianhe, came from Chengji in Longxi.

sentences.zh: 曾祖父，魏太武時以子都督討兩山屠各歿於陣，贈寧西將軍、隴西郡守。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather, in Emperor Taiwu of Wei's time as sub-commandant attacked the Liangshan Tuge and died in battle; posthumously awarded General Pacifying the West and Administrator of Longxi Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather, serving as sub-commandant under Emperor Taiwu of Wei, attacked the Liangshan Tuge and fell in battle; he was posthumously made General Pacifying the West and Administrator of Longxi Commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖斌，襲領父兵，鎮於高平，因家焉。

translations.literal: His grandfather Bin inherited his father's troops, garrisoned at Gaoping, and there made the family home.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Bin took over his father's command, garrisoned Gaoping, and settled the family there.

sentences.zh: 父文保，早卒。

translations.literal: His father Wenbao died young.
translations.idiomatic: His father Wenbao died early.

sentences.zh: 魏大統末，以賢兄弟著勳，追贈涇原東秦三州刺史、司空。

translations.literal: At the end of Western Wei Datong, because the Xian brothers had distinguished merit, posthumously enfeoffed as Governor of Jing, Yuan, and Dongqin provinces and Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Western Wei's Datong era, because the Xian brothers had won great distinction, their forebears were posthumously honored as Governors of Jing, Yuan, and Dongqin provinces and as Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 賢幼有志節，不妄舉動。

translations.literal: Xian from youth had ambition and integrity and did not act rashly.
translations.idiomatic: From boyhood Li Xian had strong character and never acted without purpose.

sentences.zh: 嘗出遊，遇一老人，鬚眉皓白，謂之曰：「我年八十，觀士多矣，未有如卿者。

translations.literal: Once on an outing he met an old man with white beard and eyebrows who said to him: "I am eighty years old; I have observed many scholars, and none have been like you.
translations.idiomatic: Once while out walking he met an old man with snow-white beard and brows who said to him: "I am eighty years old and have seen many men of talent, but none like you.

sentences.zh: 必為台牧，卿其勉之。

translations.literal: You will surely become a provincial governor—strive hard at it."
translations.idiomatic: You are destined to govern a province. Apply yourself."

sentences.zh: 」九歲，從師受業，畧觀大旨而已，不尋章句。

translations.literal: At nine years he followed a teacher to study, only skimming the main gist and not pursuing chapter and sentence analysis.
translations.idiomatic: At nine he began formal study but only grasped the broad outlines and never troubled himself with textual minutiae.

sentences.zh: 或謂之曰：「學不精勤，不如不學。

translations.literal: Someone said to him: "Study without diligence and precision—better not to study at all."
translations.idiomatic: Someone told him: "Half-hearted study is worse than none at all."

sentences.zh: 」賢曰：「夫人各有志，賢豈能彊學待問，領徒授業耶，唯當粗聞教義，補己不足。

translations.literal: Xian said: "Every man has his own aspirations—how could Xian force himself to study diligently awaiting questions, lead disciples, and teach? One should only roughly hear the teachings to supplement one's insufficiency.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xian replied: "Every man has his own path. Am I to grind away at books waiting to be questioned, or lead pupils and hold a school? I need only hear the teachings in broad outline to fill what I lack.

sentences.zh: 至如忠孝之道，實銘之於心。

translations.literal: As for the way of loyalty and filial piety, I truly engrave it in my heart."
translations.idiomatic: As for loyalty and filial piety, those I carry engraved in my heart."

sentences.zh: 」問者慙服。

translations.literal: The questioner was ashamed and convinced.
translations.idiomatic: His critic withdrew, abashed and silenced.

sentences.zh: 年十四，遭父喪，撫訓諸弟，友愛甚篤。

translations.literal: At fourteen he suffered his father's death, raised and trained his younger brothers with very deep affection.
translations.idiomatic: At fourteen, when his father died, he took charge of his younger brothers and raised them with devoted affection.

sentences.zh: 魏永安中，万俟醜奴據岐、涇等諸州反叛，魏孝莊遣爾朱天光率兵擊破之。

translations.literal: In Western Wei Yong'an, Wanqi Chounu held Qi, Jing, and other provinces in rebellion; Emperor Xiaozhuang of Wei sent Erzhu Tianguang with troops to defeat him.
translations.idiomatic: During Western Wei's Yong'an era, Wanqi Chounu rebelled and seized Qi, Jing, and neighboring provinces; Emperor Xiaozhuang of Wei sent Erzhu Tianguang to crush him.

sentences.zh: 其黨万俟道洛、費連少渾猶據原州，未知醜奴已敗。

translations.literal: His followers Wanqi Daoluo and Feilian Shaohun still held Yuan Province, not knowing Chounu had been defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Chounu's lieutenants Wanqi Daoluo and Feilian Shaohun still held Yuan Province, unaware that Chounu had already fallen.

sentences.zh: 天光遣使造賢，令密圖道洛。

translations.literal: Tianguang sent an envoy to Xian ordering him to secretly plot against Daoluo.
translations.idiomatic: Tianguang sent an envoy to Li Xian with orders to devise a secret stratagem against Daoluo.

sentences.zh: 天光率兵續進。

translations.literal: Tianguang led troops to advance in support.
translations.idiomatic: Tianguang then marched in support with his main force.

sentences.zh: 會賊黨万俟阿寶戰敗逃還，私告賢曰：「醜奴已敗，王師行至此。

translations.literal: When the rebel follower Wanqi Abao was defeated and fled back, he secretly told Xian: "Chounu has been defeated; the royal army has reached here.
translations.idiomatic: When the defeated rebel Wanqi Abao fled back to the city, he confided to Li Xian: "Chounu is beaten. The imperial army is almost upon us.

sentences.zh: 阿寶以性命相投，願能存濟。

translations.literal: Abao entrusts his life to you, hoping you can preserve and succor him."
translations.idiomatic: I stake my life on you—please find some way to save me."

sentences.zh: 」賢因令阿寶偽為醜奴使，紿道洛等曰：「今已破臺軍，須與公計事，令阿寶權守原州，公宜速往。

translations.literal: Xian thereupon had Abao pretend to be Chounu's envoy and deceive Daoluo and the others, saying: "We have now defeated the imperial army and must consult with you on affairs—Abao is temporarily guarding Yuan Province; you should go quickly."
translations.idiomatic: Li Xian then had Abao pose as Chounu's messenger and deceive Daoluo and his men: "We have routed the imperial army and need to confer with you at once. Abao will hold Yuan Province for now—you must come immediately."

sentences.zh: 」道洛等信之，是日便發。

translations.literal: Daoluo and the others believed it and set out that very day.
translations.idiomatic: Daoluo and his officers believed the story and marched out the same day.

sentences.zh: 旣出而天光至，遂克原州。

translations.literal: Once they had left, Tianguang arrived and took Yuan Province.
translations.idiomatic: As soon as they were gone, Tianguang arrived and captured Yuan Province.

sentences.zh: 道洛乃將麾下六千人奔於牽屯山。

translations.literal: Daoluo then led six thousand men under his command and fled to Qiantun Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Daoluo fled with six thousand men to Qiantun Mountain.

sentences.zh: 天光見賢曰：「道洛之出，子之力也。

translations.literal: Tianguang saw Xian and said: "Daoluo's coming out—that was your power."
translations.idiomatic: Tianguang told Li Xian: "Luring Daoluo out was your doing."

sentences.zh: 」賢又率鄉人出馬千匹以助軍，天光大悅。

translations.literal: Xian again led fellow townsmen to bring out a thousand horses to aid the army; Tianguang was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xian also rallied local men to supply a thousand horses for the army, and Tianguang was delighted.

sentences.zh: 時原州亢旱，天光以乏水草，乃退舍城東五十裏，牧馬息兵。

translations.literal: At the time Yuan Province suffered severe drought; Tianguang because of lack of grass and water withdrew and encamped fifty li east of the city to pasture horses and rest the troops.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Province was then in severe drought. Short of fodder and water, Tianguang pulled back fifty li east of the city to graze his horses and rest his men.

sentences.zh: 令都督長孫邪利行原州事，以賢為主簿。

translations.literal: He ordered Supervisor Commander Zhangsun Xieli to administer Yuan Province affairs and appointed Xian as Chief Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: He left Supervisor Commander Zhangsun Xieli in charge of the province and made Li Xian his chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 道洛復乘虛忽至，時賊黨千餘人在城中，密為內應，引道洛入城，遂殺邪利。

translations.literal: Daoluo again took advantage of emptiness and suddenly arrived; at the time over a thousand rebel followers were in the city secretly acting as inside collaborators, leading Daoluo into the city, and they then killed Xieli.
translations.idiomatic: Daoluo seized the moment and struck again. More than a thousand rebel sympathizers inside the city opened the gates, let him in, and killed Zhangsun Xieli.

sentences.zh: 賢復率鄉人殊死拒戰，道洛乃退走。

translations.literal: Xian again led fellow townsmen to fight desperately and resist; Daoluo then retreated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xian rallied the townspeople for a desperate stand and drove Daoluo back.

sentences.zh: 又有賊帥達符顯圍逼州城，晝夜攻戰，屢被摧衄。

translations.literal: There was also the rebel chief Dafu Xian who besieged and pressured the provincial city, attacking day and night and repeatedly being crushed and repulsed.
translations.idiomatic: Another rebel leader, Dafu Xian, then besieged the provincial seat and assaulted it day and night, but was beaten back again and again.

sentences.zh: 賢間道赴雍州，詣天光請援。

translations.literal: Xian took a bypath to Yong Province to see Tianguang and request reinforcements.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xian slipped through by a side route to Yong Province to beg Tianguang for relief.

sentences.zh: 天光許之，賢乃返。

translations.literal: Tianguang agreed; Xian then returned.
translations.idiomatic: Tianguang agreed, and Li Xian set out on the return journey.

sentences.zh: 而賊營壘四合，無因入城。

translations.literal: But the rebel camps closed in on four sides with no way to enter the city.
translations.idiomatic: By then the rebel camps ringed the city on every side, and there seemed no way in.

sentences.zh: 候日向夕，乃偽負薪，與賊樵采者俱得至城下。

translations.literal: Waiting until the sun was setting, he then pretended to carry firewood and, together with the rebel wood-gatherers, got to the foot of the city wall.
translations.idiomatic: At dusk he disguised himself as a woodcutter and mingled with enemy foragers until he reached the foot of the wall.

sentences.zh: 城中垂布引之，賊衆方覺，乃弓弩亂髮。

translations.literal: The city lowered cloth to pull him up; the rebel masses only then noticed and loosed bows and crossbows in chaotic volleys.
translations.idiomatic: Men inside lowered cloth and hauled him up; the rebels only then realized what was happening and loosed a wild storm of arrows.

sentences.zh: 射之不中，遂得入城，告以大軍將至。

translations.literal: The shots missed him and he thus got into the city and reported that the great army would soon arrive.
translations.idiomatic: None found their mark. He entered the city and announced that the main army was close behind.

sentences.zh: 賊聞之，便卽散走。

translations.literal: The rebels heard this and immediately dispersed and fled.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels heard it, they broke and fled at once.

sentences.zh: 累遷威烈將軍、殿中將軍、高平令。

translations.literal: Successively promoted to General of Majestic Ferocity, Palace General, and Magistrate of Gaoping.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in turn to General of Majestic Ferocity, Palace General, and Magistrate of Gaoping.

sentences.zh: 賀拔岳為侯莫陳悅所害，太祖西征。

translations.literal: He Ba Yue was killed by Houmochen Yue; Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai marched west in expedition.
translations.idiomatic: When He Ba Yue was murdered by Houmochen Yue, Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai marched west to punish him.

sentences.zh: 賢與其弟遠、穆等密應侯莫陳崇。

translations.literal: Xian with his younger brother Yuan, Mu, and others secretly responded to Houmochen Chong.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xian, his younger brother Li Yuan, Mu, and others secretly joined Houmochen Chong in the uprising.

sentences.zh: 以功授都督，仍守原州。

translations.literal: For merit he was granted Supervisor status and still guarded Yuan Province.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he was made a supervisor and kept on as garrison commander of Yuan Province.

sentences.zh: 及大軍將至秦州，悅棄城走，太祖令兄子導勒兵追之，以賢為前驅。

translations.literal: When the grand army was about to reach Qin Province, Yue abandoned the city and fled; Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai ordered his nephew's son Dao to lead troops in pursuit, with Xian as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: As the main force neared Qin Province, Yue abandoned the city and fled. Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai sent his grandnephew Dao in pursuit with Li Xian as vanguard.

sentences.zh: 轉戰四百餘里，至牽屯山及之，悅自剄於陣。

translations.literal: Fighting over more than four hundred li, at Qiantun Mountain they caught up; Yue cut his own neck in battle.
translations.idiomatic: After more than four hundred li of fighting they caught Yue at Qiantun Mountain, where he slit his own throat on the field.

sentences.zh: 賢亦被重瘡，馬中流矢。

translations.literal: Xian also received grievous wounds and his horse was hit by a flowing arrow.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xian himself was badly wounded, and his horse took a stray arrow.

sentences.zh: 太祖嘉之，賞奴婢、布帛及雜畜等，授持節、撫軍大將軍、都督。

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai praised him, rewarded him with male and female slaves, cloth, silk, and assorted livestock, and granted Staff Bearer, Grand General Pacifying the Army, and Supervisor status.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai commended him, gave him slaves, cloth, silk, and livestock, and appointed him Staff Bearer, Grand General Pacifying the Army, and supervisor.

sentences.zh: 魏孝武西遷，太祖令賢率騎兵迎衛。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu of Wei migrated west, Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai ordered Xian to lead cavalry to welcome and escort him.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu of Wei moved west, Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai ordered Li Xian to ride out with cavalry to receive and escort him.

sentences.zh: 時山東之衆，多欲逃歸。

translations.literal: At the time many of the eastern troops wanted to flee back home.
translations.idiomatic: Many of the eastern soldiers then wanted to desert and go home.

sentences.zh: 帝乃令賢以精騎三百為殿，衆皆憚之，莫敢亡叛。

translations.literal: The Emperor then ordered Xian with three hundred elite cavalry as rearguard; all feared them and none dared to desert or rebel.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor put Li Xian at the rear with three hundred picked horsemen. The men feared him, and none dared to bolt.

sentences.zh: 封下邽縣公，邑一千戶。

translations.literal: Enfeoffed as Duke of Xiagi county with a fief of one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed as Duke of Xiagi with a fief of one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 俄授左都督、安東將軍，還鎮原州。

translations.literal: Soon granted Left Supervisor, General Pacifying the East, and returned to garrison Yuan Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Left Supervisor and General Pacifying the East and returned to garrison Yuan Province.

sentences.zh: 大統二年，州民豆盧狼害都督大野樹兒等，據州城反。

translations.literal: In the second year of Datong, provincial people Dou Lu Lang killed Supervisors Daye Shu'er and others and, holding the provincial city, rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Datong, a local man named Dou Lu Lang murdered Supervisors Daye Shu'er and others, seized the provincial city, and rebelled.

sentences.zh: 賢乃招集豪傑與之謀曰：「賊起倉卒，便誅二將，其勢雖盛，其志已驕。

translations.literal: Xian then gathered bold heroes and counseled with them, saying: "The rebels rose in sudden haste and at once executed two generals—though their force is mighty, their will is already arrogant.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xian gathered local leaders and laid out his plan: "These rebels struck in haste and killed two commanders. Their numbers look strong, but success has already made them reckless.

sentences.zh: 然其政令莫施，唯以殘剝為業。

translations.literal: Yet their government orders are not carried out; they take only cruel plunder as their occupation.
translations.idiomatic: They govern by nothing but terror and looting.

sentences.zh: 夫以羇旅之賊，而馭烏合之衆，勢自離解。

translations.literal: With transient bandits driving a mob gathered by chance, the force by itself will split and dissolve.
translations.idiomatic: Outsiders ruling a mob that came together by chance—such a force will fall apart on its own.

sentences.zh: 今若從中擊之，賊必喪膽。

translations.literal: If we now strike them from within, the rebels will surely lose their courage.
translations.idiomatic: Strike them from inside now and they will lose heart.

sentences.zh: 如吾計者，指日取之。

translations.literal: As I plan it, we shall take them within days."
translations.idiomatic: Do as I say and we will have them within days."

sentences.zh: 」衆皆從焉。

translations.literal: All followed him.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone agreed.

sentences.zh: 賢乃率敢死士三百人，分為兩道，乘夜鼓噪而出。

translations.literal: Xian then led three hundred dare-to-die men divided into two routes and, taking advantage of night with drum and clamor, burst out.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xian then led three hundred volunteers in two columns and, under cover of night with drums and shouts, charged out.

sentences.zh: 羣賊大驚，一戰而敗，狼乃斬關遁走。

translations.literal: The rebel masses were greatly alarmed and were defeated in one battle; Lang then broke through the gate and fled.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels panicked and broke in a single clash. Dou Lu Lang cut his way out and fled.

sentences.zh: 賢輕與三騎追斬之。

translations.literal: Xian lightly with three riders pursued and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xian pursued with only three horsemen, caught him, and cut off his head.

sentences.zh: 遷原州長史，尋行原州事。

translations.literal: Promoted to Chief Clerk of Yuan Province; soon acting in Yuan Province affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to chief clerk of Yuan Province and soon given charge of provincial affairs.

sentences.zh: 四年，莫折後熾連結賊黨，所在寇掠。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, Mozhe Houchi allied with rebel bands and everywhere raided and plundered.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, Mozhe Houchi joined with rebel bands and ravaged the countryside.

sentences.zh: 賢率鄉兵與行涇州事史寧討之。

translations.literal: Xian led local troops with Shi Ning, acting governor of Jing Province, to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xian marched with local levies alongside Shi Ning, acting governor of Jing Province, to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 後熾列陣以待。

translations.literal: Houchi deployed formation to await them.
translations.idiomatic: Houchi drew up his lines and waited.

sentences.zh: 賢謂寧曰：「賊聚結歲久，徒衆甚多，數州之人，皆為其用。

translations.literal: Xian said to Ning: "The rebels have gathered and allied for years; their followers are very numerous; people of several provinces all serve them.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xian told Ning: "These rebels have been gathering strength for years. Their ranks are huge, and men from several provinces fight for them.

sentences.zh: 我若總一陣併力擊之，彼旣同惡相濟，理必總萃於我。

translations.literal: If I concentrate into one formation and combine strength to strike them, since they are alike in evil and aid each other, they will surely by principle all mass against me.
translations.idiomatic: If we mass every man into one battle line, they will rally to one another and throw their whole weight against us.

sentences.zh: 其勢不分，衆寡莫敵。

translations.literal: Their force undivided, I cannot match them in numbers.
translations.idiomatic: United, they will outnumber us beyond hope.

sentences.zh: 我便救尾，無以制之。

translations.literal: Even if I rescue the tail, I cannot control them.
translations.idiomatic: Even chasing their rear we could not bring them to heel.

sentences.zh: 今若令諸軍分為數隊，多設旗鼓，掎角而前，以脅諸柵。

translations.literal: Now if we order the various armies divided into several columns with many flags and drums, advancing in pincer angles to pressure the various stockades—
translations.idiomatic: Instead, split our forces into several columns with many flags and drums and advance in pincers to threaten each stockade—

sentences.zh: 公別統精兵，直指後熾，按甲而待，莫與交鋒。

translations.literal: You separately command elite troops directly toward Houchi, hold armor and wait, do not engage in combat.
translations.idiomatic: while you take the elite straight at Houchi, hold your ground, and refuse battle.

sentences.zh: 後熾欲前，則憚公之銳。

translations.literal: When Houchi wishes to advance, he will then fear your sharpness.
translations.idiomatic: Houchi will not dare advance for fear of your crack troops.

sentences.zh: 諸柵欲出，則懼我疑兵。

translations.literal: When the stockades wish to come out, they will fear our feigned troops.
translations.idiomatic: The stockades will not dare sally out for fear of our decoy columns.

sentences.zh: 令其進不得戰，退不得走，以候其懈，擊之必破。

translations.literal: Making them unable to advance to fight, unable to retreat and flee—we wait for their slackness and strike them, and they will surely be broken.
translations.idiomatic: Hem them in so they can neither fight nor flee. When their guard slackens, strike—and they will break.

sentences.zh: 後熾一敗，則衆柵不攻自拔矣。

translations.literal: Once Houchi is defeated once, the many stockades need no attack and will fall of themselves."
translations.idiomatic: Once Houchi falls, the rest of the stockades will collapse without a blow."

sentences.zh: 」寧不從，屢戰頻北。

translations.literal: Ning did not follow and repeatedly fought and frequently lost northward.
translations.idiomatic: Ning refused the plan, fought head-on again and again, and kept losing.

sentences.zh: 賢乃率數百騎徑掩後熾營，收其妻子、僮隸五百餘人，並輜重等。

translations.literal: Xian then led several hundred cavalry directly to raid Houchi's camp and seized his wives, children, and retainers—more than five hundred persons—along with baggage and supplies.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xian then led several hundred horsemen in a direct raid on Houchi's camp and captured his wives, children, and retainers—more than five hundred people—together with baggage and supplies.

sentences.zh: 屬後熾與寧戰勝，方欲追奔，忽聞賢至，乃棄寧與賢接戰。

translations.literal: It happened that Houchi had defeated Ning in battle and was just about to pursue the fleeing—suddenly hearing Xian had arrived, he then abandoned Ning and met Xian in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Houchi had just beaten Ning and was about to pursue when word came that Li Xian was upon him. He broke off against Ning and turned to fight Li Xian.

sentences.zh: 賢手斬十餘級，生獲六人，賊遂大敗。

translations.literal: Xian personally beheaded more than ten heads and captured six alive; the rebels then suffered great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xian personally killed more than ten men and took six alive. The rebels were routed.

sentences.zh: 後熾單騎遁走。

translations.literal: Houchi fled alone on one horse.
translations.idiomatic: Houchi escaped alone on horseback.

sentences.zh: 師還，以功賞奴婢四十口，雜畜數百頭。

translations.literal: When the army returned, for merit he was rewarded with forty male and female slaves and several hundred head of assorted livestock.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned, he was rewarded with forty slaves and several hundred head of livestock for his service.

sentences.zh: 八年，授原州刺史。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, granted Governor of Yuan Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was appointed Governor of Yuan Province.

sentences.zh: 賢雖少從戎旅，而頗閑政事，撫導鄉里，甚得民和。

translations.literal: Though Xian from youth followed the military, he was quite versed in government affairs, comforting and guiding the hometown folk, very much winning the people's harmony.
translations.idiomatic: Though Li Xian had soldiered since youth, he understood civil administration well, cared for his home district, and won deep goodwill among the people.

sentences.zh: 十二年，隨獨孤信征涼州，平之。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, he followed Dugu Xin in expedition to Liang Province and pacified it.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he followed Dugu Xin on campaign to Liang Province and helped pacify it.

sentences.zh: 又撫慰張掖等五郡而還。

translations.literal: He again comforted and reassured Zhangye and the other five commanderies and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He then pacified Zhangye and four neighboring commanderies before returning.

sentences.zh: 俄而茹茹圍逼州城，剽掠居民，驅擁畜牧。

translations.literal: Soon the Ruru besieged and pressured the provincial city, plundering residents and driving off livestock.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward the Ruru besieged the provincial seat, looting the people and driving off herds.

sentences.zh: 賢欲出戰，大都督王德猶豫未決。

translations.literal: Xian wished to go out and fight; Grand Supervisor Wang De hesitated and had not decided.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xian wanted to sally out and fight, but Grand Supervisor Wang De wavered and could not decide.

sentences.zh: 賢固請，德乃從之。

translations.literal: Xian firmly requested; De then followed him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xian pressed hard for action, and Wang De at last agreed.

sentences.zh: 賢勒兵將出，賊密知之，乃引軍退。

translations.literal: Xian drew up troops about to go out; the rebels secretly knew it and then led the army to withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xian formed his men to march out, but the enemy learned of it in advance and began to pull back.

sentences.zh: 賢因率騎士追擊，斬二百餘級，捕虜百餘人，獲駞馬牛羊二萬頭，財物不可勝計。

translations.literal: Xian thereupon led knights in pursuit, beheading more than two hundred heads and capturing more than a hundred prisoners, obtaining more than twenty thousand camels, horses, cattle, and sheep, with goods and wealth beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xian then led cavalry in pursuit, killed more than two hundred men, took more than a hundred prisoners, and recovered more than twenty thousand camels, horses, cattle, and sheep, with loot beyond reckoning.

sentences.zh: 所掠之人，還得安堵。

translations.literal: The people who had been plundered again obtained peace and settlement.
translations.idiomatic: The people who had been robbed were able to live in peace again.

sentences.zh: 加授使持節、車騎大將軍、儀同三司。

translations.literal: Additionally granted Staff Bearer, Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, and Equal in Three Departments.
translations.idiomatic: He was further granted Staff Bearer, Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, and Equal in Three Departments.

sentences.zh: 十六年，遷驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, promoted to Grand General of Fast Cavalry and General of the Grand Office, Equal in Three Departments.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he was promoted to Grand General of Fast Cavalry and General of the Grand Office, Equal in Three Departments.

sentences.zh: 太祖之奉魏太子西巡也，至原州，遂幸賢第，讓齒而坐，行鄉飲酒禮焉。

translations.literal: When Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai escorted the Wei crown prince on a western tour, arriving at Yuan Province, he then visited Xian's residence, gave way by age in seating, and performed the village drinking rite.
translations.idiomatic: When Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai escorted the Wei crown prince on a tour of the west and reached Yuan Province, he visited Li Xian's home, yielded the senior seat by age, and shared the village drinking ceremony with him.

sentences.zh: 其後，太祖又至原州，令賢乘輅，備儀服，以諸侯會遇禮相見，然後幸賢第，歡宴終日。

translations.literal: Afterwards, Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai again came to Yuan Province, ordered Xian to ride in a chariot with full ceremonial dress, and they met with the ceremonial reception accorded feudal lords; only then did he visit Xian's residence and feast joyfully all day.
translations.idiomatic: Later Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai came to Yuan Province again, had Li Xian ride in state with full ceremonial dress, and received him with the honors due a feudal lord before visiting his home and feasting with him all day.

sentences.zh: 凡是親族，頒賜有差。

translations.literal: All his close kin received graded bestowal.
translations.idiomatic: Every member of his clan received gifts according to rank.

sentences.zh: 魏恭帝元年，進爵河西郡公，增邑通前二千戶。

translations.literal: In the first year of Emperor Gong of Wei, advanced in rank to Duke of Hexi Commandery with fief increased with the previous to two thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Emperor Gong of Wei he was raised to Duke of Hexi Commandery, his fief rising to two thousand households in all.

sentences.zh: 後以弟子植被誅，賢坐除名。

translations.literal: Later because his nephew Zhi was executed, Xian was punished by removal from the registers.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when his nephew Zhi was put to death, Li Xian was stripped of rank and office as kin punishment.

sentences.zh: 俄授使持節、車騎大將軍、儀同三司。

translations.literal: Soon granted Staff Bearer, Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, and Equal in Three Departments.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon reappointed Staff Bearer, Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, and Equal in Three Departments.

sentences.zh: 時荊州羣蠻反，開府潘招討之。

translations.literal: At that time the various barbarians of Jing Province rebelled; Opening-Office Pan was ordered to campaign against them.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the barbarian peoples of Jing Province rose in revolt, and Pan of the Opening Office was sent to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 令賢與賀若敦率騎士七千，別道邀截，擊蠻帥文子榮，大破之。

translations.literal: Xian was ordered with He Ruo Dun to lead seven thousand horsemen by a separate route to intercept, attack the barbarian chief Wen Zirong, and inflict a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xian and He Ruo Dun were ordered to take seven thousand horsemen by a side road, intercept the barbarian chief Wen Zirong, and rout him completely.

sentences.zh: 遂於平州北築汶陽城以鎮之。

translations.literal: They then built Wenyang city north of Ping Province to garrison the region.
translations.idiomatic: They then built Wenyang city north of Ping Province to hold the area.

sentences.zh: 尋治郢州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Governor of Ying Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Governor of Ying Province.

sentences.zh: 時以巴、湘初附，詔賢總監諸軍，畧定，乃遷江夏民二千餘戶以實安州，幷築甑山城而還。

translations.literal: At that time, because Ba and Xiang had just submitted, an edict ordered Xian to oversee all armies and secure the region; he then moved more than two thousand households from Jiangxia to populate An Province, also built Zengshan city, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Because Ba and Xiang had only recently submitted, an edict put Li Xian in overall command of the armies to pacify the region. He then resettled more than two thousand households from Jiangxia to fill out An Province, built Zengshan fort, and returned.

sentences.zh: 保定二年，詔復賢官爵，仍授瓜州刺史。

translations.literal: In the second year of Baoding, an edict restored Xian's rank and title and again appointed him Governor of Gua Province.
translations.idiomatic: In Baoding 2 an edict restored Li Xian's rank and title and reappointed him Governor of Gua Province.

sentences.zh: 高祖及齊王憲之在繈褓也，以避忌，不利居宮中。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu and Prince of Qi Yuwen Hu were still in swaddling clothes, to avoid taboo it was inauspicious for them to live in the palace.
translations.idiomatic: While Emperor Gaozu and Prince of Qi Yuwen Hu were still infants, taboo made it inauspicious for them to remain in the palace.

sentences.zh: 太祖令于賢家處之，六載乃還宮。

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai had them lodged at Yu Xian's household; only after six years did they return to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai had them stay at Li Xian's home, and only after six years did they return to the palace.

sentences.zh: 因賜賢妻吳姓宇文氏，養為侄女，賜與甚厚。

translations.literal: Thereupon he gave Xian's wife, née Wu, the surname Yuwen, raised her as his niece, and bestowed on them very generously.
translations.idiomatic: He then gave Li Xian's wife, née Wu, the surname Yuwen, treated her as his own niece, and lavished gifts upon them.

sentences.zh: 及高祖西巡，幸賢第，詔曰：「朕昔沖幼，爰寓此州。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu toured the west and visited Xian's residence, an edict said: "In my youth I was placed in this province.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozu toured the west and visited Li Xian's home, he issued an edict: "In my childhood I lived in this province.

sentences.zh: 使持節、驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司、大都督、瓜州諸軍事、瓜州刺史賢，斯土良家，勳德兼著，受委居朕，輔導積年。

translations.literal: Staff Bearer, Grand General of Fast Cavalry, Equal in Three Departments with Opening Office, Grand Governor-General, Commander of Gua military affairs, and Governor of Gua Xian—of this land's good families, with both merit and virtue outstanding, entrusted to dwell with me, guiding and instructing for many years.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xian—Staff Bearer, Grand General of Fast Cavalry, Equal in Three Departments with Opening Office, Grand Governor-General, commander of Gua military affairs, and Governor of Gua—came from a fine local family, won distinction in both merit and virtue, was entrusted to live with me, and guided me for many years.

sentences.zh: 念其規弼，功勞甚茂。

translations.literal: Reflecting on his counsel and support, his labor and merit are very abundant.
translations.idiomatic: Thinking of his guidance and support, his service has been abundant indeed.

sentences.zh: 食彼桑椹，尚懷好音，矧茲惠矣，其庸可忘？

translations.literal: Eating those mulberries, one still cherishes the good sound—how much more this kindness; how could it be forgotten?
translations.idiomatic: One who ate mulberries there still remembers the place fondly—how much more should I remember such kindness? How could I forget it?

sentences.zh: 今巡撫居此，不殊代邑，舉目依然，益增舊想。

translations.literal: Now touring and comforting this place where I dwell, it is no different from my old home; every sight is as before, increasing old memories all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Now, touring the place where I once lived, it is no different from my old home. Every sight is unchanged, and my old memories grow all the stronger.

sentences.zh: 雖無屬籍，朕處之若親。

translations.literal: Though without kinship in the registers, I treat him as close kin.
translations.idiomatic: Though he is not kin by the registers, I treat him as family.

sentences.zh: 凡厥昆季乃至子侄等，可並豫宴賜。

translations.literal: All his brothers and younger brothers down to sons and nephews may together share in the feast and bestowal.
translations.idiomatic: All his brothers and nephews alike shall share in the feast and gifts.

sentences.zh: 」於是令中侍上士尉遲愷往瓜州，降璽書勞賢，賜衣一襲及被褥，幷御所服十三環金帶一要、中廄馬一匹、金裝鞍勒、雜彩五百段、銀錢一萬。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he ordered Attendant Palace Gentleman Yuchi Kai to go to Gua Province, deliver an imperial letter commending Xian, and bestow one suit of clothing and bedding, together with one thirteen-ring gold belt worn by the emperor himself, one horse from the central stud, gold-mounted saddle and bridle, five hundred bolts of assorted silks, and ten thousand in silver cash.
translations.idiomatic: " He then sent Attendant Palace Gentleman Yuchi Kai to Gua Province with an imperial letter of commendation for Li Xian, together with a suit of clothes and bedding, the emperor's own thirteen-ring gold belt, a horse from the imperial stables with gold-mounted saddle and bridle, five hundred bolts of colored silk, and ten thousand in silver cash.

sentences.zh: 賜賢弟申國公穆亦如之。

translations.literal: Xian's younger brother Duke of Shen Mu received the same.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xian's younger brother Mu, Duke of Shen, received the same.

sentences.zh: 子侄男女中外諸孫三十四人，各賜衣一襲。

translations.literal: Thirty-four sons, daughters, nephews, nieces, and grandchildren by both maternal and paternal lines each received one suit of clothing.
translations.idiomatic: Thirty-four sons, daughters, nephews, nieces, and grandchildren on both sides of the family each received a suit of clothes.

sentences.zh: 又拜賢甥厙狄樂為儀同。

translations.literal: He also appointed Xian's nephew Kudil Le as Equal in Protocol.
translations.idiomatic: He also made Li Xian's nephew Kudil Le an Equal in Protocol.

sentences.zh: 賢門生昔經侍奉者，二人授大都督，四人授帥都督，六人別將。

translations.literal: Of Xian's former disciples who had once served him, two were appointed Grand Governors-General, four were appointed Command Governors-General, and six were made Separate Generals.
translations.idiomatic: Of Li Xian's former disciples who had once attended him, two were made Grand Governors-General, four Command Governors-General, and six Separate Generals.

sentences.zh: 奴已免賤者，五人授軍主，未免賤者十二人酬替放之。

translations.literal: Of slaves already freed from base status, five were appointed Army Chiefs; twelve not yet freed from base status were compensated and released.
translations.idiomatic: Of his slaves already freed from servile status, five were made Army Chiefs; twelve still in servile status were compensated and manumitted.

sentences.zh: 四年，王師東討，朝議以西道空虛，慮羌、渾侵擾，乃授賢使持節、河州總管、三州七防諸軍事、河州刺史。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, when the royal army campaigned east, court discussion held that the western route was empty and feared Qiang and Hun raids; Xian was thereupon appointed Staff Bearer, Area Commander of He Province, Commander of the military affairs of three provinces and seven garrisons, and Governor of He Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, when the royal army marched east, the court feared the western frontier was exposed to Qiang and Hun raids and appointed Li Xian Staff Bearer, area commander of He Province, commander of three provinces and seven garrisons, and Governor of He.

sentences.zh: 河州舊非總管，至是創置焉。

translations.literal: He Province had formerly not had an area command; at this time one was newly established.
translations.idiomatic: He Province had never before had an area command; one was now created for the first time.

sentences.zh: 賢乃大營屯田，以省運漕；

translations.literal: Xian then greatly developed garrison farming to economize on transport by canal;
translations.idiomatic: Li Xian then greatly expanded garrison farming to cut the cost of grain transport;

sentences.zh: 多設斥候，以備寇戎。

translations.literal: he set up many scouts to guard against enemy raiders.
translations.idiomatic: and posted many scouts to guard against enemy raids.

sentences.zh: 於是羌、渾斂迹，不敢向東。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Qiang and Hun restrained themselves and did not dare turn east.
translations.idiomatic: The Qiang and Hun thereupon kept quiet and did not dare move east.

sentences.zh: 五年，宕昌寇邊，百姓失業，乃於洮州置總管府以鎮遏之。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, Tanchang raided the frontier and the people lost their livelihoods; a headquarters of area command was then established at Tao Province to suppress and restrain them.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year Tanchang raided the border, leaving the people destitute, and an area-command headquarters was set up at Tao Province to hold them down.

sentences.zh: 遂廢河州總管，改授賢洮州總管、七防諸軍事，洮州刺史。

translations.literal: The He area command was then abolished, and Xian was reassigned as Area Commander of Tao, Commander of the military affairs of seven garrisons, and Governor of Tao Province.
translations.idiomatic: The He area command was abolished, and Li Xian was reassigned area commander of Tao, commander of seven garrisons, and Governor of Tao.

sentences.zh: 屬羌寇石門戍，撤破橋道，以絕援軍，賢率千騎禦之，前後斬獲數百人，賊乃退走。

translations.literal: It happened that the Qiang raided Shimen garrison, tore up and destroyed bridges and roads to cut off relief troops; Xian led a thousand horsemen to resist them, beheading and capturing several hundred men before and after, and the bandits then retreated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: When the Qiang attacked Shimen garrison, destroyed bridges and roads to cut off relief, Li Xian met them with a thousand horsemen, killed and captured several hundred men in successive clashes, and drove the enemy off.

sentences.zh: 羌復引吐谷渾數千騎，將入西疆。

translations.literal: The Qiang again brought in several thousand horsemen of Tuyuhun, about to enter the western frontier.
translations.idiomatic: The Qiang then brought in several thousand Tuyuhun horsemen to invade the western frontier.

sentences.zh: 賢密知之，又遣兵伏其隘路，復大敗之。

translations.literal: Xian secretly learned of it and again sent troops to ambush them on the narrow road, inflicting another great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xian learned of it in secret and sent troops to ambush them on the pass, inflicting another great defeat.

sentences.zh: 虜遂震懾，不敢犯塞。

translations.literal: The enemy thereupon were awed and did not dare violate the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy were terrified and no longer dared raid the border.

sentences.zh: 俄廢洮州總管，還於河州置總管府，復以賢為之。

translations.literal: Soon the Tao area command was abolished; the area-command headquarters was restored at He Province, and Xian was again made its commander.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the Tao area command was abolished, the headquarters was restored at He Province, and Li Xian was again put in command.

sentences.zh: 高祖思賢舊恩，征拜大將軍。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu, mindful of Xian's old kindness, summoned and appointed him Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: Mindful of Li Xian's old kindness, Emperor Gaozu summoned him and made him Grand General.

sentences.zh: 天和四年三月，卒於京師，時年六十八。

translations.literal: In the third month of the fourth year of Tianhe, he died in the capital; he was sixty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of Tianhe 4 he died in the capital at the age of sixty-eight.

sentences.zh: 高祖親臨，哀動左右。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu came in person; his grief moved those around him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu came in person to mourn him, and his grief moved all who were present.

sentences.zh: 贈使持節、柱國大將軍、大都督、涇原秦等十州諸軍事、原州刺史。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted Staff Bearer, Pillar-of-State Grand General, Grand Governor-General, Commander of the military affairs of ten provinces including Jing, Yuan, and Qin, and Governor of Yuan Province.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was granted Staff Bearer, Pillar-of-State Grand General, Grand Governor-General, commander of the military affairs of ten provinces including Jing, Yuan, and Qin, and Governor of Yuan.

sentences.zh: 諡曰桓。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Huan.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous title was Huan ("Steadfast").

sentences.zh: 子端嗣。

translations.literal: His son Duan succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: His son Duan succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 端字永貴，歷位開府儀同三司、司會中大夫、中州刺史。

translations.literal: Duan, styled Yonggui, successively held the posts of Equal in Three Departments with Opening Office, Palace Master of the Department of Accounts, and Governor of Zhong Province.
translations.idiomatic: Duan, styled Yonggui, rose through the posts of Equal in Three Departments with Opening Office, Palace Master of the Department of Accounts, and Governor of Zhong.

sentences.zh: 從高祖平齊，於鄴城戰歿，贈上大將軍，追封襄陽公，諡曰果。

translations.literal: Following Emperor Gaozu in pacifying Qi, he died in battle at Ye city; posthumously granted Upper Grand General, posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Xiangyang, posthumous title Guo.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Emperor Gaozu in the conquest of Qi and fell in battle at Ye; posthumously he was made Upper Grand General, enfeoffed as Duke of Xiangyang, and given the posthumous title Guo ("Resolute").

sentences.zh: 端弟吉，儀同三司。

translations.literal: Duan's younger brother Ji held Equal in Three Departments.
translations.idiomatic: Duan's younger brother Ji held Equal in Three Departments.

sentences.zh: 吉弟崇，位至太府中大夫、上柱國、廣宗郡公。

translations.literal: Ji's younger brother Chong reached the posts of Palace Master of the Treasury Department, Upper Pillar-of-State, and Duke of Guangzong Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Ji's younger brother Chong rose to Palace Master of the Treasury Department, Upper Pillar-of-State, and Duke of Guangzong.

sentences.zh: 崇弟孝軌，開府儀同大將軍、升遷縣伯。

translations.literal: Chong's younger brother Xiaogui was Grand General Equal in Three Departments with Opening Office and Baron of Shengqian county.
translations.idiomatic: Chong's younger brother Xiaogui was Grand General Equal in Three Departments with Opening Office and Baron of Shengqian.

sentences.zh: 孝軌弟詢，少歷顯位。

translations.literal: Xiaogui's younger brother Xun, from youth successively held eminent posts.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaogui's younger brother Xun held high office from an early age.

sentences.zh: 大象末，上柱國、隴西郡公。

translations.literal: At the end of the Daxiang reign, he was Upper Pillar-of-State and Duke of Longxi Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Daxiang reign he was Upper Pillar-of-State and Duke of Longxi.

sentences.zh: 賢弟遠，字萬歲。

translations.literal: Xian's younger brother Yuan, styled Wansui.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xian's younger brother Li Yuan, styled Wansui.

sentences.zh: 幼有器局，志度恢然。

translations.literal: From youth he had capacity and breadth of vision; his will and bearing were expansive.
translations.idiomatic: From boyhood he had breadth of mind and a commanding presence.

sentences.zh: 嘗與羣兒為戰鬥之戲，指麾部分，便有軍陣之法。

translations.literal: Once, playing at battle with a group of boys, he directed and deployed them, and there was already the method of army formations.
translations.idiomatic: Once, while playing at war with other boys, he deployed them in ranks with the discipline of a real army.

sentences.zh: 郡守見而異之，召使更戲。

translations.literal: The commandery administrator saw this and was struck by it; he summoned him to play again.
translations.idiomatic: The commandery administrator saw it, marveled at it, and had him perform again.

sentences.zh: 羣兒懼而散走，遠持杖叱之，復為向勢，意氣雄壯，殆甚於前。

translations.literal: The boys were afraid and scattered and fled; Yuan held a staff and shouted at them, again forming the forward disposition; his spirit was bold and strong, almost greater than before.
translations.idiomatic: The boys panicked and ran off, but Yuan seized a staff, shouted them back into line, and re-formed the advance with even bolder spirit than before.

sentences.zh: 郡守曰：「此小兒必為將軍，非常人也。

translations.literal: The commandery administrator said: "This boy will surely become a general—a man out of the ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: The commandery administrator said: "This boy is destined to become a general. He is no ordinary child.

sentences.zh: 」及長，涉獵書傳，畧知指趣而已。

translations.literal: " When grown, he ranged through books and records, only roughly knowing their main purport.
translations.idiomatic: " When he grew up he read widely in books and records, but knew only their general drift.

sentences.zh: 魏正光末，天下鼎沸，勒勒賊胡琮侵逼原州，其徒甚盛。

translations.literal: At the end of Zhengguang of Wei, the realm boiled like a cauldron; the Lele bandit Hu Cong invaded and pressed on Yuan Province, and his followers were very numerous.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Wei's Zhengguang era the realm was in turmoil; the Lele bandit Hu Cong pressed on Yuan Province with a very large following.

sentences.zh: 遠昆季率勵鄉人，欲圖拒守，而衆情猜懼，頗有異同。

translations.literal: Yuan and his brothers led and encouraged the townspeople, wishing to plan defense and hold out, but public sentiment was suspicious and fearful, with much disagreement.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuan and his brothers rallied the townspeople to hold the city, but the people were fearful and divided in opinion.

sentences.zh: 遠乃按劍而言曰：「頃年以來，皇家多難。

translations.literal: Yuan then grasped his sword and spoke, saying: "In recent years the royal house has suffered many calamities.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuan then drew his sword and said: "In recent years the dynasty has suffered one disaster after another.

sentences.zh: 匈黨乘機，肆其毒螫。

translations.literal: The Hun faction seized the opportunity and vented their poison and sting.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel factions seized the moment and spread their poison.

sentences.zh: 王畧未振，緩其梟夷。

translations.literal: Imperial strategy had not yet recovered momentum, and their execution was delayed.
translations.idiomatic: The throne has not yet restored its authority, and their punishment has been postponed.

sentences.zh: 正是忠臣立節之秋，義士建功之日。

translations.literal: This is exactly the season for loyal ministers to establish their integrity and for men of righteousness to achieve merit.
translations.idiomatic: This is precisely the time for loyal ministers to stand firm and for men of honor to win distinction.

sentences.zh: 丈夫豈可臨難苟免，當在死中求生耳。

translations.literal: How can a man facing hardship seek only to escape? One must seek life within death.
translations.idiomatic: How can a man facing danger think only of saving himself? One must find life in the midst of death.

sentences.zh: 諸人並世載忠貞，沐浴教義，今若棄同卽異，去順效逆，雖五尺童子，猶或非之，將復何顏以見天下之士。

translations.literal: You all for generations have borne loyalty and fidelity, bathed in righteous teaching; if now you abandon unity and take separate paths, leave the lawful and imitate rebellion—even a boy five feet tall would still disapprove; with what face could you again meet the gentlemen of the realm?
translations.idiomatic: Your families have been loyal for generations and steeped in duty. If you now abandon unity, turn from the lawful course, and follow rebellion—even a child would condemn you. What face would you show the men of honor under Heaven?

sentences.zh: 有異議者，請以劔斬之！

translations.literal: Whoever has a different opinion, let him be struck down with the sword!
translations.idiomatic: Anyone who disagrees, let him be cut down where he stands!

sentences.zh: 」於是衆皆股栗，莫不聽命。

translations.literal: " Thereupon the crowd all trembled in their thighs and none failed to obey.
translations.idiomatic: " At that everyone trembled with fear, and none dared disobey.

sentences.zh: 乃相與盟歃，遂深壁自守。

translations.literal: They then swore alliance together and deeply walled themselves in for defense.
translations.idiomatic: They swore a common oath, strengthened the walls, and held out.

sentences.zh: 而外無救援，城遂陷。

translations.literal: But outside there was no relief, and the city then fell.
translations.idiomatic: No relief came from outside, and the city fell.

sentences.zh: 其徒多被殺害，唯遠兄弟並為人所匿，得免。

translations.literal: Most of their followers were killed; only the Yuan brothers were hidden by others and escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Most of their followers were slaughtered; only Li Yuan and his brothers were hidden by others and survived.

sentences.zh: 遠乃言於賢曰：「今逆賊孔熾，屠戮忠良。

translations.literal: Yuan then spoke to Xian, saying: "Now the rebel bandits blaze fiercely and slaughter the loyal and good.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuan then said to Li Xian: "The rebels now run rampant and butcher the loyal.

sentences.zh: 遠欲間行入朝，請兵救援。

translations.literal: Yuan wishes to go by secret route to court and request troops for relief.
translations.idiomatic: I mean to slip through the enemy lines to court and beg for relief troops.

sentences.zh: 兄晦跡和光，可以免禍。

translations.literal: Elder brother, conceal your traces and harmonize with the light—you can thereby escape disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Brother, keep a low profile and bide your time—you can escape harm that way.

sentences.zh: 內伺釁隙，因變立功。

translations.literal: Within, watch for an opening; by change achieve merit.
translations.idiomatic: Watch from within for an opening, and strike when the moment comes.

sentences.zh: 若王師西指，得復表裏相應，旣殉國家之急，且全私室之危。

translations.literal: If the royal army points west, we can again respond inside and out; thus serving the state's urgent need and also preserving our private household's peril.
translations.idiomatic: When the royal army marches west, we can coordinate from within and without—serving the state in its crisis and saving our family as well.

sentences.zh: 豈若窘迫凶威，坐見夷滅！

translations.literal: How is that like being pressed by brutal power and sitting to watch extermination!
translations.idiomatic: Surely that is better than cowering under the enemy and waiting to be destroyed!

sentences.zh: 」賢曰：「是吾心也。

translations.literal: " Xian said: "That is my heart too.
translations.idiomatic: " Li Xian said: "That is exactly what I feel.

sentences.zh: 」遂定東行之策。

translations.literal: " They thereupon fixed the plan to go east.
translations.idiomatic: " They then settled on the plan for Li Yuan to go east.

sentences.zh: 遠乃崎嶇寇境，得達京師。

translations.literal: Yuan then traversed the rugged enemy territory and reached the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuan then made his way through enemy-held country by a hard road and reached the capital.

sentences.zh: 魏朝嘉之，授武騎常侍。

translations.literal: The Wei court commended him and appointed him Regular Palace Attendant of Martial Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei court praised him and made him Regular Palace Attendant of Martial Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 俄轉別將，賜帛千匹，幷弓刀衣馬等。

translations.literal: Soon transferred to Separate General; granted one thousand bolts of silk, together with bow, blade, clothing, horse, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Separate General and given a thousand bolts of silk, together with bow, blade, clothing, and horse.

sentences.zh: 及爾朱天光西伐，乃配遠精兵，使為鄉導。

translations.literal: When Erzhu Tianguang campaigned west, he then assigned Yuan picked troops and made him native guide.
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Tianguang marched west, he gave Li Yuan picked troops and made him guide through the country.

sentences.zh: 天光欽遠才望，特相引接，除伏波將軍、長城郡守、原州大中正。

translations.literal: Tianguang admired Yuan's talent and reputation and especially drew him close, appointing him General Who Quells the Waves, Administrator of Changcheng Commandery, and Chief Rectifier of Yuan Province.
translations.idiomatic: Tianguang admired Li Yuan's talent and reputation, treated him with special favor, and made him General Who Quells the Waves, Administrator of Changcheng, and Chief Rectifier of Yuan Province.

sentences.zh: 後以應侯莫陳崇功，遷高平郡守。

translations.literal: Later, for responding to Houmochen Chong's merit, he was transferred to Administrator of Gaoping Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Later, for his service under Houmochen Chong, he was transferred to Administrator of Gaoping.

sentences.zh: 太祖見遠，與語悅之，令居麾下，甚見親遇。

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai saw Yuan, spoke with him and was pleased, ordered him to dwell under his command, and treated him with great personal favor.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai met Li Yuan, spoke with him, and was pleased; he kept him in his own service and treated him with marked favor.

sentences.zh: 及魏孝武西遷，授假節、銀青光祿大夫、主衣都統，封安定縣伯，邑五百戶。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu of Wei migrated west, he was granted provisional staff, Silver Seal Blue-Girdle Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Chief of the Imperial Wardrobe Corps, enfeoffed as Baron of Anding county with a fief of five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu of Wei moved west, Li Yuan was granted provisional staff, Silver Seal Blue-Girdle Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Chief of the Imperial Wardrobe Corps, and enfeoffed Baron of Anding with five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 魏文帝嗣位之始，思享遐年，以遠字可嘉，令扶帝升殿。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Wen of Wei's accession, wishing to enjoy long years, because Yuan's style name was commendable, he ordered him to support the emperor up the hall steps.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Wen of Wei's reign, wishing long life for himself and finding Li Yuan's style name auspicious, he had him support the emperor up the hall steps.

sentences.zh: 遷使持節、征東大將軍，進爵為公，增邑千戶，仍領左右。

translations.literal: Transferred to Staff Bearer and Grand General Pacifying the East; advanced in rank to duke, fief increased by one thousand households; still leading the Left and Right.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Staff Bearer and Grand General Pacifying the East, raised to duke with an added fief of one thousand households, and continued to command the Left and Right.

sentences.zh: 從征竇泰，復弘農，並有殊勳。

translations.literal: Following in campaigns against Dou Tai and in recovering Hongnong, in both he had outstanding merit.
translations.idiomatic: He followed campaigns against Dou Tai and in the recovery of Hongnong, distinguishing himself in both.

sentences.zh: 授都督、原州刺史。

translations.literal: Appointed Governor-General and Governor of Yuan Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Governor-General and Governor of Yuan Province.

sentences.zh: 太祖謂遠曰：「孤之有卿，若身體之有手臂之用，豈可暫輟於身。

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai said to Yuan: "My having you is like the body having the use of arms and legs—how could I briefly do without you on my person?
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai said to Li Yuan: "Having you is like having arms and legs—how can I do without you even for a moment?

sentences.zh: 本州之榮，乃私事耳。

translations.literal: The glory of this province is only a private matter.
translations.idiomatic: The honor of governing this province is a private matter.

sentences.zh: 卿若述職，則孤無所寄懷。

translations.literal: If you go to your post, then I have nowhere to place my trust.
translations.idiomatic: If you leave to take up your post, I have nowhere to turn.

sentences.zh: 」於是遂令遠兄賢代行州事。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he ordered Yuan's elder brother Xian to act in provincial affairs in his stead.
translations.idiomatic: " He then had Li Yuan's elder brother Li Xian act as governor in his place.

sentences.zh: 沙苑之役，遠功居最，除車騎大將軍、儀同三司，進爵陽平郡公，邑三千戶。

translations.literal: At the battle of Shayuan, Yuan's merit ranked first; he was appointed Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry and Equal in Three Departments, advanced in enfeoffment to Duke of Yangping Commandery with a fief of three thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: At Shayuan Li Yuan's merit ranked first; he was made Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry and Equal in Three Departments, and raised to Duke of Yangping with a fief of three thousand households.

sentences.zh: 尋從獨孤信東畧，遂入洛陽。

translations.literal: Soon following Dugu Xin in eastern campaign, he then entered Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: He soon followed Dugu Xin on an eastern campaign and entered Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 為東魏將侯景等所圍。

translations.literal: He was besieged by Eastern Wei generals Hou Jing and others.
translations.idiomatic: There he was besieged by Eastern Wei generals led by Hou Jing.

sentences.zh: 太祖至，乃解。

translations.literal: When Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai arrived, the siege was then lifted.
translations.idiomatic: When Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai arrived, the siege was lifted.

sentences.zh: 及河橋之戰，遠與獨孤信為右軍，不利而退。

translations.literal: At the battle of River Bridge, Yuan with Dugu Xin formed the right wing; the battle went badly and they withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: At the River Bridge battle Li Yuan and Dugu Xin commanded the right wing; the fight went badly and they withdrew.

sentences.zh: 除大丞相府司馬。

translations.literal: Appointed Chief Clerk of the Grand Chancellor's Office.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Chief Clerk of the Grand Chancellor's Office.

sentences.zh: 軍國機務，遠皆參之，畏避權勢，若不在己。

translations.literal: In military and state urgent affairs Yuan participated in all of them, fearing and avoiding power as if it were not his own.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in all urgent military and state affairs, yet shunned power as if it were not his to grasp.

sentences.zh: 時河東初復，民情未安，太祖謂遠曰：「河東國之要鎮，非卿無以撫之。

translations.literal: At that time Hedong had just been recovered and the people's hearts were not yet settled; Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai said to Yuan: "Hedong is a key fortress of the state—without you there is no one to pacify it.
translations.idiomatic: Hedong had just been recovered and the people were still unsettled. Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai said to Li Yuan: "Hedong is a vital fortress of the state. No one but you can pacify it.

sentences.zh: 」乃授河東郡守。

translations.literal: " He thereupon appointed him Administrator of Hedong Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: " He then made Li Yuan Administrator of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 遠敦獎風俗，勸課農桑，肅遏姦非，兼修守禦之備。

translations.literal: Yuan encouraged customs and rewarded worthy conduct, urged the people in farming and sericulture, sternly checked wickedness and wrongdoing, and together with this repaired the defenses for guarding and fighting.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuan encouraged good customs, promoted farming and sericulture, sternly checked crime, and strengthened the defenses.

sentences.zh: 曾未期月，百姓懷之。

translations.literal: Before a full month had passed, the common people cherished him.
translations.idiomatic: In less than a month the people had come to love him.

sentences.zh: 太祖嘉焉，降書勞問。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor commended this and sent down a letter of praise and inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai commended this and sent a letter of praise and inquiry.

sentences.zh: 征為侍中、驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: He was summoned as attendant-in-ordinary, grand general of rapid cavalry, and opening-office equal-to-three-division protocol.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as attendant-in-ordinary, grand general of rapid cavalry, and opening-office equal-to-three-division protocol.

sentences.zh: 魏建東宮，授太子少傅，尋轉少師。

translations.literal: When Wei established the Eastern Palace, he was appointed junior preceptor to the crown prince; soon he was transferred to junior mentor.
translations.idiomatic: When Western Wei established the Eastern Palace, he was appointed junior preceptor to the crown prince and soon transferred to junior mentor.

sentences.zh: 東魏北豫州刺史高仲密請舉州來附。

translations.literal: Eastern Wei's governor of North Yu Province, Gao Zhongmi, requested to surrender the whole province and come over.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Zhongmi, Eastern Wei's governor of North Yu Province, offered to surrender his province and defect.

sentences.zh: 時齊神武屯兵河陽。

translations.literal: At that time Qi Divine Warrior Gao Huan had encamped his troops at Hene.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Gao Huan had encamped at Hene.

sentences.zh: 太祖以仲密所據遼遠，難為應接，諸將皆憚此行。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor, because Zhongmi's position was distant and remote, found it hard to support him, and all the generals feared this expedition.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai thought Zhongmi's position too distant to support easily, and all the generals feared the mission.

sentences.zh: 遠曰：「北豫遠在賊境，高歡又屯兵河陽，常理而論，實難救援。

translations.literal: Yuan said: "North Yu lies far in enemy territory, and Gao Huan again has troops encamped at Hene; by ordinary reasoning, rescue is truly hard.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuan said: "North Yu lies deep in enemy territory, and Gao Huan holds Hene; by ordinary reckoning rescue is nearly impossible.

sentences.zh: 但兵務神速，事貴合機。

translations.literal: But military affairs require speed, and affairs value seizing the moment.
translations.idiomatic: But war demands speed, and success depends on timing.

sentences.zh: 古人有言：『不入獸穴，安得獸子。

translations.literal: The ancients had a saying: 'If you do not enter the beast's den, how can you get the beast's cub?
translations.idiomatic: The ancients said: "If you do not enter the beast's den, how can you take the beast's cub?

sentences.zh: 』若以奇兵出其不意，事或可濟。

translations.literal: ' If with a surprise force one strikes where they do not expect, the affair may perhaps succeed.
translations.idiomatic: " If we strike with a surprise force where they do not expect, the affair may yet succeed.

sentences.zh: 脫有利鈍，故是兵家之常。

translations.literal: If there should be gain or loss, that is the constant way of military men.
translations.idiomatic: Gain or loss is the common lot of war.

sentences.zh: 如其顧望不行，便無克定之日。

translations.literal: If one hesitates and does not go, there will never be a day of pacification.
translations.idiomatic: If we hesitate and do not go, there will never be a day of victory.

sentences.zh: 」太祖喜曰：「李萬歲所言，差強人意。

translations.literal: " The Grand Progenitor was pleased and said: "What Li Wan Sui has said is rather to one's liking.
translations.idiomatic: " Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai was pleased and said: "What Li Wan Sui has said is rather to my liking.

sentences.zh: 」乃授行臺尚書，前驅東出。

translations.literal: " He thereupon appointed him director of the mobile secretariat and sent him east as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: " He thereupon made him director of the mobile secretariat and sent him east as vanguard.

sentences.zh: 太祖率大軍繼進。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor led the great army in continued advance.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai followed with the main army.

sentences.zh: 遠乃潛師而往，拔仲密以歸。

translations.literal: Yuan then moved his force secretly, went, and brought Zhongmi back after taking him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuan then marched secretly, extracted Zhongmi, and brought him back.

sentences.zh: 仍從太祖戰于邙山。

translations.literal: He again followed the Grand Progenitor in fighting at Mount Mang.
translations.idiomatic: He again followed Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai in the battle at Mount Mang.

sentences.zh: 時大軍不利，遠獨整所部為殿。

translations.literal: At that time the great army fared badly; Yuan alone put his command in order and served as rearguard.
translations.idiomatic: When the main army was beaten, Li Yuan alone kept his command in order and covered the retreat.

sentences.zh: 尋授都督義州弘農等二十一防諸軍事。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed area commander over the military affairs of the twenty-one garrisons of Yi Province, Hongnong, and the rest.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made area commander over the twenty-one garrisons of Yi Province, Hongnong, and the rest.

sentences.zh: 遠善綏撫，有幹畧，守戰之備，無不精銳。

translations.literal: Yuan was good at soothing and comforting, had capacity and strategy, and in preparations for defense and battle nothing was not sharp and keen.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuan was skilled at winning people over, had capacity and strategy, and his defenses and battle preparations were all sharp and thorough.

sentences.zh: 每厚撫〔境〕外〔之〕人，使為間謀，敵中動靜，必先知之。

translations.literal: Each time he treated people beyond the border generously and had them serve as spies; enemy movements within their camp he always knew first.
translations.idiomatic: He generously treated people beyond the border and used them as spies, so he always learned enemy movements first.

sentences.zh: 至有事泄被誅戮者，亦不以為悔。

translations.literal: Even when some whose affairs leaked out were executed, he did not regard it as regret.
translations.idiomatic: Even when some spies were exposed and executed, he did not regret it.

sentences.zh: 其得人心如此。

translations.literal: In winning hearts he was like this.
translations.idiomatic: Such was his hold on men's hearts.

sentences.zh: 嘗校獵於莎柵，見石於叢蒲中，以為伏兔，射之而中，鏃入寸餘。

translations.literal: Once when reviewing a hunt at Sha Stockade, he saw a stone in thick reeds, took it for a crouching rabbit, shot it and hit it, and the arrowhead entered more than an inch.
translations.idiomatic: Once while reviewing a hunt at Sha Stockade he saw a stone in thick reeds, took it for a crouching rabbit, shot it, and drove the arrowhead more than an inch into the stone.

sentences.zh: 就而視之，乃石也。

translations.literal: Going up to look, it was a stone.
translations.idiomatic: When he went to look, it was a stone.

sentences.zh: 太祖聞而異之，賜書曰：「昔李將軍廣親有此事，公今復爾，可謂世載其德。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor heard and marveled at it, and granted a letter saying: "In old times General Li Guang himself had this affair; you now again do the same—one may say the virtue is carried generation after generation.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai heard and marveled, and wrote: "Long ago General Li Guang himself had this feat; you now repeat it—truly the virtue runs in the family.

sentences.zh: 雖熊渠之名，不能獨擅其美。」

translations.literal: Though the name of Xiongqu cannot alone monopolize the beauty."
translations.idiomatic: Even the fame of Xiongqu cannot claim the honor alone."

sentences.zh: 東魏將段孝先率步騎二萬趨宜陽，以送糧為名，然實有窺窬之意。

translations.literal: Eastern Wei general Duan Xiaoxian led twenty thousand foot and horse toward Yiyang, in name to deliver grain, but in fact with intent to encroach.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Wei general Duan Xiaoxian led twenty thousand infantry and cavalry toward Yiyang, ostensibly to deliver grain but in fact with designs on the region.

sentences.zh: 遠密知其計，遣兵襲破之，獲其輜重器械。

translations.literal: Yuan secretly knew his plan, sent troops in a surprise attack and broke him, and captured his baggage train and equipment.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuan learned his plan in secret, sent troops to surprise and rout him, and captured his baggage train and equipment.

sentences.zh: 孝先遁走。

translations.literal: Xiaoxian fled and went away.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoxian fled.

sentences.zh: 太祖乃賜所乘馬及金帶床帳衣被等，幷雜彩二千匹，拜大將軍。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor thereupon granted the horse he himself rode, together with a gold belt, bed curtains, clothing and bedding, and also two thousand bolts of mixed silks, and appointed him grand general.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai thereupon granted his own horse, a gold belt, bed curtains, clothing and bedding, and two thousand bolts of mixed silks, and made him grand general.

sentences.zh: 頃之，除尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: Before long, he was removed and made left vice director of the secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was made left vice director of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 遠白太祖曰：「遠，秦隴匹夫，才藝俱爾。

translations.literal: Yuan told the Grand Progenitor: "Yuan is a common man of Qin and Long; talent and skill are alike modest.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuan told Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai: "I am a common man of Qin and Long, no greater in talent or skill than any other.

sentences.zh: 平生念望，不過一郡守耳。

translations.literal: All my life my hopes have gone no farther than a single commandery governor.
translations.idiomatic: All my life I hoped for nothing beyond a single commandery governorship.

sentences.zh: 遭逢際會，得奉聖明。

translations.literal: Meeting with the right moment, I was able to serve the sage and bright.
translations.idiomatic: Meeting the right moment, I was able to serve a sage ruler.

sentences.zh: 主貴臣遷，以至於此。

translations.literal: When the lord is honored the minister is promoted, and so it has come to this.
translations.idiomatic: When the lord is honored the minister rises, and so it has come to this.

sentences.zh: 今位居上列，爵邁通侯，受委方面，生殺在手。

translations.literal: Now I stand in the upper ranks, my nobility surpasses full marquis, I am entrusted with a frontier command, and life and death are in my hand.
translations.idiomatic: Now I stand among the highest ranks, my title outranks a full marquis, I hold a frontier command, and life and death are in my hands.

sentences.zh: 非直榮寵一時，亦足光華身世。

translations.literal: It is not only glory and favor for a moment—it is also enough to brighten body and generation.
translations.idiomatic: That is not only honor for a moment—it also brings glory to my house.

sentences.zh: 但尚書僕射，任居端揆，今以賜授，適所以重其罪責。

translations.literal: But the vice director of the secretariat holds a post at the head of government; to grant it now only adds weight to the charge and blame.
translations.idiomatic: But the vice director of the secretariat stands at the head of government; to grant it now only adds to my burden of blame.

sentences.zh: 明公若欲全之，乞寢此授。

translations.literal: If Your Illustrious Grace wishes to preserve me, I beg that this appointment be withdrawn.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Grace wishes to preserve me, I beg that this appointment be withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 」太祖曰：「公勳德兼美，朝廷欽屬，選衆而舉，何足為辭。

translations.literal: " The Grand Progenitor said: "Your merit and virtue are both fine; the court admires and relies on you; chosen from the multitude and raised up—what is there to decline?
translations.idiomatic: " Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai said: "Your merit and virtue are both outstanding; the court admires and relies on you; you were chosen from the multitude—what is there to decline?

sentences.zh: 且孤之於公，義等骨肉，豈容於官位之間，便致退讓，深乖所望也。

translations.literal: Moreover, between me and you the bond is like flesh and bone—how could I allow you, over mere office and rank, to yield and withdraw? That would deeply miss what I hope for.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, between us the bond is like flesh and bone—how could I allow you to yield over mere office and rank? That would deeply disappoint me.

sentences.zh: 」遠不得已，方拜職。

translations.literal: " Yuan had no choice and then accepted the post.
translations.idiomatic: " Li Yuan had no choice and accepted the post.

sentences.zh: 太祖又以第十一子達令遠子之，卽代王也。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor also had his eleventh son Da become Yuan's adopted son—this was the Prince of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai also had his eleventh son Yuwen Da become Li Yuan's adopted son—this was the Prince of Dai.

sentences.zh: 其見親待如此。

translations.literal: In being treated with intimacy he was like this.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the intimacy with which he was treated.

sentences.zh: 時太祖嫡嗣未建，明帝居長，已有成德；

translations.literal: At that time the Grand Progenitor's primary heir had not yet been established; Emperor Ming, though eldest, already had mature virtue;
translations.idiomatic: At that time Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai's primary heir had not yet been established; Emperor Ming, though eldest, already showed mature virtue;

sentences.zh: 孝閔處嫡，年尚幼沖。

translations.literal: Xiaomin stood in the position of the primary wife's son, but his years were still very young.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaomin was the son of the primary wife, but he was still very young.

sentences.zh: 乃召羣公謂之曰：「孤欲立子以嫡，恐大司馬有疑。

translations.literal: He then summoned the assembled lords and said to them: "I wish to establish a son by the primary wife; I fear the Grand Marshal may have doubts.
translations.idiomatic: He then summoned the assembled lords and said: "I wish to establish a son by the primary wife; I fear the grand marshal may have doubts.

sentences.zh: 」大司馬卽獨孤信，明帝敬後父也。

translations.literal: " The Grand Marshal was Dugu Xin, father of Emperor Ming's empress.
translations.idiomatic: " The grand marshal was Dugu Xin, father of Emperor Ming's empress.

sentences.zh: 衆皆默，未有言者，遠曰：「夫立子以嫡不以長，禮經明義。

translations.literal: All were silent and none spoke; Yuan said: "In establishing a son, one takes the primary wife's son, not the eldest—the Rites Classic makes the principle clear.
translations.idiomatic: All were silent; Li Yuan said: "In establishing a son, one takes the primary wife's son, not the eldest—the Rites make the principle clear.

sentences.zh: 畧陽公為世子，公何所疑。

translations.literal: Duke Jue of Lueyang should be heir apparent—what doubt has Your Grace?
translations.idiomatic: Duke Jue of Lueyang should be heir apparent—what doubt has Your Grace?

sentences.zh: 若以信為嫌，請卽斬信。

translations.literal: If Xin is taken as the cause for suspicion, I ask to cut off Xin at once.
translations.idiomatic: If Xin is the problem, I ask to cut off Xin at once.

sentences.zh: 」便拔刀而起。

translations.literal: " He then drew his sword and rose.
translations.idiomatic: " He then drew his sword and rose.

sentences.zh: 太祖亦起曰：「何事至此！

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor also rose and said: "What affair has come to this!
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai also rose and said: "What affair has come to this!

sentences.zh: 」信又自陳說，遠乃止。

translations.literal: " Xin again explained himself, and Yuan then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: " Xin again explained himself, and Li Yuan then stopped.

sentences.zh: 於是羣公並從遠議。

translations.literal: Thereupon all the assembled lords followed Yuan's proposal.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon all the assembled lords followed Li Yuan's proposal.

sentences.zh: 出外拜謝信曰：「臨大事，不得不爾。

translations.literal: Going outside he bowed in apology to Xin and said: "Facing a great affair, one cannot do otherwise.
translations.idiomatic: Going outside he bowed in apology to Xin and said: "Facing a great affair, one cannot do otherwise.

sentences.zh: 」信亦謝遠曰：「今日賴公，決此大議。

translations.literal: " Xin also apologized to Yuan and said: "Today I rely on you to decide this great deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: " Xin also apologized to Li Yuan and said: "Today I rely on you to decide this great deliberation.

sentences.zh: 」六官建，授小司寇。

translations.literal: " When the Six Offices were established, he was appointed minor minister of justice.
translations.idiomatic: " When the Six Offices were established, he was appointed minor minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 孝閔帝踐阼，進位柱國大將軍，邑千戶。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaomin took the throne, he was advanced to pillar of state and grand general, with a fief of one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaomin took the throne, he was advanced to pillar of state and grand general, with a fief of one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 復鎮弘農。

translations.literal: He again garrisoned Hongnong.
translations.idiomatic: He again garrisoned Hongnong.

sentences.zh: 遠子植，在太祖時已為相府司錄參軍，掌朝政。

translations.literal: Yuan's son Zhi, already in the Grand Progenitor's time, had been director of records in the chancellor's office and controlled court government.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuan's son Li Zhi had already served in Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai's time as director of records in the chancellor's office and controlled court government.

sentences.zh: 及晉公護執權，恐不被任用，乃密欲誅護。

translations.literal: When Duke Yuwen Hu of Jin seized power, fearing he would not be employed, he secretly wished to kill Hu.
translations.idiomatic: When Duke Yuwen Hu of Jin seized power, fearing he would not be employed, Li Zhi secretly plotted to kill Hu.

sentences.zh: 語在《孝閔帝紀》。

translations.literal: The account is in the Records of Emperor Xiaomin.
translations.idiomatic: The account is in the Records of Emperor Xiaomin.

sentences.zh: 謀頗漏泄，護知之，乃出植為梁州刺史。

translations.literal: The plot largely leaked out; Hu learned of it and thereupon sent Zhi out as governor of Liang Province.
translations.idiomatic: The plot largely leaked out; Hu learned of it and sent Li Zhi out as governor of Liang Province.

sentences.zh: 尋而廢帝，召遠及植還朝。

translations.literal: Soon afterward the emperor was deposed; Yuan and Zhi were summoned back to court.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward the emperor was deposed; Li Yuan and Li Zhi were summoned back to court.

sentences.zh: 遠恐有變，沉吟久之，乃曰：「大丈夫寧為忠鬼，安能作叛臣乎！

translations.literal: Yuan feared there would be trouble, hesitated long, and then said: "A great man would rather be a loyal ghost—how could he become a rebel minister!
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuan feared trouble, hesitated long, and then said: "A great man would rather be a loyal ghost—how could he become a rebel minister!

sentences.zh: 」遂就徵。

translations.literal: " He thereupon answered the summons.
translations.idiomatic: " He thereupon answered the summons.

sentences.zh: 旣至京師，護以遠功名素重，猶欲全宥之。

translations.literal: When he reached the capital, Hu, because Yuan's fame and merit had long been weighty, still wished to spare him.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached the capital, Hu, because Li Yuan's fame and merit had long been weighty, still wished to spare him.

sentences.zh: 乃引與相見，謂之曰：「公兒遂有異謀，非止屠戮護身，乃是傾危宗社。
