translations.literal: He then led him in to meet and said to him: "Your son indeed had a different plot—not only to slaughter Hu's person but to overturn the altars of soil and grain.
translations.idiomatic: He then led him in to meet and said: "Your son indeed had a different plot—not only to kill me but to overturn the state.

sentences.zh: 叛臣賊子，理宜同疾，公可早為之所。

translations.literal: Rebel ministers and traitor sons by right should share the hatred—you may act early against him.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel ministers and traitor sons by right should share the hatred—you may act early against him.

sentences.zh: 」乃以植付遠。

translations.literal: " He then handed Zhi over to Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: " He then handed Li Zhi over to Li Yuan.

sentences.zh: 遠素鍾愛於植，植又口辯，乃云初無此謀。

translations.literal: Yuan had always loved Zhi deeply; Zhi was also glib of tongue and declared he had had no such plot at first.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuan had always loved Li Zhi deeply; Li Zhi was also glib and declared he had had no such plot at first.

sentences.zh: 遠謂為信然。

translations.literal: Yuan took it as true.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuan believed him.

sentences.zh: 詰朝，將植謁護，護謂植已死，乃曰：「陽平公何意乃自來也？

translations.literal: At dawn the next day he was about to lead Zhi to call on Hu; Hu thought Zhi was already dead and then said: "Duke of Yangping, what intent is this that you have come yourself?
translations.idiomatic: At dawn the next day he was about to lead Li Zhi to call on Hu; Hu thought Li Zhi was already dead and said: "Duke of Yangping, what intent is this that you have come yourself?

sentences.zh: 」左右云：「植亦在門外。

translations.literal: " Attendants said: "Zhi is also outside the gate.
translations.idiomatic: " Attendants said: "Li Zhi is also outside the gate.

sentences.zh: 」護大怒曰：「陽平公不信我矣！

translations.literal: " Hu was greatly angry and said: "Duke of Yangping no longer trusts me!
translations.idiomatic: " Hu was furious and said: "Duke of Yangping no longer trusts me!

sentences.zh: 」乃召入，仍命遠同坐，令帝與植相質於遠前。

translations.literal: " He then summoned them in, still ordered Yuan to sit together, and had the emperor and Zhi confront each other before Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: " He then summoned them in, ordered Li Yuan to sit with him, and had the emperor and Li Zhi confront each other before Li Yuan.

sentences.zh: 植辭窮，謂帝曰：「本為此謀，欲安社稷，利至尊耳。

translations.literal: Zhi's words were exhausted; he said to the emperor: "This plot was originally to settle the altars of soil and grain and benefit the supreme one alone.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhi was cornered; he said to the emperor: "This plot was originally to settle the realm and benefit Your Majesty alone.

sentences.zh: 今日至此，何事云云。

translations.literal: Today it has come to this—what is all this talk.
translations.idiomatic: Today it has come to this—what is all this talk.

sentences.zh: 」遠聞之，自投於床曰：「若爾，誠合萬死。

translations.literal: " Yuan heard it and threw himself on the bed, saying: "If so, you truly deserve ten thousand deaths.
translations.idiomatic: " Li Yuan heard it and threw himself on the bed, saying: "If so, you truly deserve ten thousand deaths.

sentences.zh: 」於是護乃害植，幷逼遠令自殺。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Hu killed Zhi and also forced Yuan to kill himself.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon Hu killed Li Zhi and also forced Li Yuan to kill himself.

sentences.zh: 時年五十一。

translations.literal: He was then fifty-one years old.
translations.idiomatic: He was then fifty-one years old.

sentences.zh: 植弟叔諧、叔謙、叔讓亦死。

translations.literal: Zhi's younger brothers Shuxie, Shuqian, and Shurang also died.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhi's younger brothers Shuxie, Shuqian, and Shurang also died.

sentences.zh: 餘並以年幼得免。

translations.literal: The rest were all spared because they were young.
translations.idiomatic: The rest were all spared because they were young.

sentences.zh: 植弟基，字仲和。

translations.literal: Zhi's younger brother Ji, styled Zhonghe.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhi's younger brother Li Ji, styled Zhonghe.

sentences.zh: 幼有聲譽，美容儀，善談論，涉獵羣書，尤工騎射。

translations.literal: In youth he had reputation, fine bearing and appearance, was skilled in discussion, ranged widely through many books, and was especially adept at mounted archery.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he had a fine reputation, handsome bearing, skill in debate, wide reading, and especial mastery of mounted archery.

sentences.zh: 太祖召見奇之，乃令尚義歸公主。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor summoned and saw him, marveled at him, and had him marry Princess Yigui.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai summoned him, marveled at him, and had him marry Princess Yigui.

sentences.zh: 大統十年，釋褐員外散騎常侍。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Datong he began his career as supernumerary regular attendant of the scattered cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Datong he entered service as supernumerary regular attendant of the scattered cavalry.

sentences.zh: 後以父勳，封建安縣公，邑一千戶。

translations.literal: Later, because of his father's merit, he was enfeoffed Duke of Jiang'an county with a fief of one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Later, because of his father's merit, he was enfeoffed Duke of Jiang'an county with a fief of one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 累遷撫軍將軍、銀青光祿大夫、通直散騎常侍，領大丞相親信。

translations.literal: By cumulative promotion he became general who pacifies the army, grand master with silver-blue-golden-light seal, regular attendant through direct connection of the scattered cavalry, and head of the grand chancellor's personal staff.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to general who pacifies the army, grand master with silver-blue-golden-light seal, regular attendant through direct connection of the scattered cavalry, and head of the grand chancellor's personal staff.

sentences.zh: 俄轉大都督、進爵清河郡公。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to grand commander and advanced in nobility to Duke of Qinghe commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made grand commander and raised to Duke of Qinghe commandery.

sentences.zh: 太祖扶危定傾，威權震主，及魏廢帝卽位之後，猜隙彌深。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor supported the endangered and settled the tottering; his authority and power awed the ruler; and after the deposed Wei emperor took the throne, suspicion and rifts grew ever deeper.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai had supported the endangered realm and awed the throne; after the deposed Wei emperor succeeded, suspicion and rifts grew ever deeper.

sentences.zh: 時太祖諸子，年皆幼沖，章武公導、中山公護復東西作鎮，唯托意諸婿，以為心膂。

translations.literal: At that time all the Grand Progenitor's sons were still very young; Duke Dao of Zhangwu and Duke Hu of Zhongshan were again posted east and west on command; he relied only on his sons-in-law as his inner guard.
translations.idiomatic: At that time all Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai's sons were still very young; Duke Dao of Zhangwu and Duke Hu of Zhongshan were posted on distant commands east and west; he relied only on his sons-in-law as his inner guard.

sentences.zh: 基與義城公李暉、常山公于翼等俱為武衛將軍，分掌禁旅。

translations.literal: Ji together with Li Hui, Duke of Yicheng, Yu Yi, Duke of Changshan, and the rest were all martial-guard generals, each commanding part of the forbidden troops.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ji together with Li Hui, Duke of Yicheng, Yu Yi, Duke of Changshan, and the rest were all martial-guard generals, each commanding part of the palace guard.

sentences.zh: 帝深憚之，故密謀遂泄。

translations.literal: The emperor deeply feared them, and so the secret plot thereupon leaked out.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor deeply feared them, and so the secret plot leaked out.

sentences.zh: 魏恭帝卽位，遷使持節、車騎大將軍、儀同三司，加散騎常侍，進爵燉煌郡公，尋加侍中、驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司，拜陽平國世子。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gong of Wei took the throne, he was transferred to commissioner with full credentials, grand general of chariots and cavalry, equal-to-three-division protocol, given the added post of regular attendant of the scattered cavalry, advanced in nobility to Duke of Dunhuang commandery, soon given the added posts of attendant-in-ordinary, grand general of rapid cavalry, and opening-office equal-to-three-division protocol, and appointed heir of Yangping state.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gong of Wei took the throne, he was made commissioner with full credentials, grand general of chariots and cavalry with equal-to-three-division protocol, given regular attendant of the scattered cavalry, raised to Duke of Dunhuang commandery, soon given attendant-in-ordinary, grand general of rapid cavalry, and opening-office equal-to-three-division protocol, and appointed heir of Yangping state.

sentences.zh: 六官建，授御正中大夫。

translations.literal: When the Six Offices were established, he was appointed grand master of imperial rectification.
translations.idiomatic: When the Six Offices were established, he was appointed grand master of imperial rectification.

sentences.zh: 孝閔帝踐阼，出為海州刺史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaomin acceded, he was sent out as governor of Haizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaomin acceded, Li Ji was posted out as governor of Haizhou.

sentences.zh: 威字安民，起家右侍上士，累遷至開府儀同三司，又改襲遠爵陽平郡公。

translations.literal: Wei, styled Anmin, began as right attending upper gentleman, was repeatedly promoted to opening-office equal-in-three-departments, and then changed to inherit Yuan's title as Duke of Yangping Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Li Wei, styled Anmin, entered service as right attending upper gentleman, rose in stages to opening-office equal-in-three-departments, and then took over Yuan's title as Duke of Yangping.

sentences.zh: 從高祖平齊，以功授上開府、拜軍司馬。

translations.literal: Following Emperor Gaozu in pacifying Qi, for merit he was awarded upper opening-office and appointed army vice marshal.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Emperor Gaozu in the conquest of Qi and, for merit, was given upper opening-office and made army vice marshal.

sentences.zh: 宣帝卽位，進授大將軍，出為熊州刺史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuan acceded, he was advanced to grand general and sent out as governor of Xiongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuan acceded, he was raised to grand general and posted out as governor of Xiongzhou.

sentences.zh: 大象末，位至柱國。

translations.literal: At the end of the Daxiang era, his rank reached pillar of state.
translations.idiomatic: By the end of the Daxiang era he had reached pillar of state.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：李賢和兄弟，屬亂離之際，居戎馬之間，志畧縱橫，忠勇奮發，亟摧勍敵，屢涉艱危，而功未書於王府，仕不過於州郡。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: Li Xianhe and his brothers, amid disorder and separation, lived among campaigns and horses; their plans were far-ranging, their loyalty and courage ardent; they repeatedly crushed formidable foes and often passed through peril—yet their merit was not recorded in the princely house, and their offices did not exceed prefecture and commandery.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer writes: Li Xianhe and his brothers lived through civil collapse amid constant warfare; bold in design and fierce in loyalty, they repeatedly broke strong enemies and often faced mortal danger—yet their achievements went unrecorded at court, and their posts never rose above the prefectural level.

sentences.zh: 及逢時值主，策名委質，或使煩莫府，或契闊戎行，荷生成之恩，蒙國士之遇，俱縻好爵，各著勳庸。

translations.literal: When they met the right time and ruler, they registered their names and pledged allegiance; some were repeatedly burdened at headquarters, some shared long campaigns in the field; they bore the grace of their upbringing and received treatment as national champions; all held fine ranks and each won distinction.
translations.idiomatic: When fortune and a worthy sovereign came together, they pledged their service: some were repeatedly called to headquarters, others spent years on campaign; nourished by imperial favor and honored as men of the realm, they all held high rank and each earned a record of merit.

sentences.zh: 遂得任兼文武，聲彰內外，位高望重，光國榮家，跗萼連暉，椒聊繁衍，冠冕之盛，當時莫比焉。

translations.literal: Thus they held civil and military office together, their fame resounding within and without, their rank high and their weight heavy; they glorified the state and honored their houses—calyxes joined in radiance, pepper-sprigs flourishing—the splendor of caps and robes, none in their day could compare.
translations.idiomatic: They came to hold both civil and military posts, their fame ringing at court and abroad, their standing lofty and their weight immense; they brought glory to the state and honor to their clans, their branches flourishing together in a brilliance of rank and office unmatched in their time.

sentences.zh: 自周迄隋，鬱為西京盛族，雖金、張在漢，不之尚也。

translations.literal: From Zhou through Sui they were a great clan of the Western Capital; even the Jin and Zhang of Han cannot be held above them.
translations.idiomatic: From Northern Zhou through Sui they stood as one of the great families of the Western Capital—a splendor that not even the Jin and Zhang clans of Han could surpass.

sentences.zh: 然而太祖初崩，嗣君沖幼。

translations.literal: Yet when Grand Progenitor first died, the heir was young and tender.
translations.idiomatic: Yet when Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai first died, the successor was still a child.

sentences.zh: 內則功臣放命，外則強寇臨邊。

translations.literal: Within, meritorious ministers acted on their own authority; without, strong enemies pressed the borders.
translations.idiomatic: Within the court, meritorious ministers grew insubordinate; on the frontier, powerful foes pressed the borders.

sentences.zh: 晉公以猶子之親，膺負圖之托，遂能撫寧家國，開翦異端，革魏興周，遠安邇悅。

translations.literal: Duke of Jin, by the closeness of a foster son, received the trust of the Mandate; he was able to soothe and settle house and realm, open paths and cut down heterodox elements, change Wei and raise Zhou, bring distant peace and near contentment.
translations.idiomatic: Duke of Jin Yuwen Hu, as a foster son bound by close kinship, shouldered the trust of the imperial charge; he pacified house and realm, cleared away opposition, overthrew Wei and raised Zhou, and won peace far and near.

sentences.zh: 功勤已著，過惡未彰。

translations.literal: Merit and diligence were already manifest; faults and crimes not yet revealed.
translations.idiomatic: His achievements were already plain; his faults had not yet come to light.

sentences.zh: 李植受遇先朝，宿參機務，恐威權之已去，懼將來之不容，生此厲階，成茲貝錦，乃以小謀大，由疎間親。

translations.literal: Li Zhi had received favor in the previous reign and long participated in confidential affairs; fearing that authority had already passed from him and dreading no tolerance in what was to come, he created this step to disaster and wove this embroidered slander—using small means to plot against great, through estrangement dividing kin.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhi, favored under the previous reign and long privy to state secrets, feared that power had already slipped from his hands and that the future would not spare him; he opened the way to disaster and spun a web of slander—plotting from weakness against strength and driving a wedge between close kin.

sentences.zh: 主無昭帝之明，臣有上官之訴。

translations.literal: The ruler lacked Emperor Zhao's clarity; the minister had Shangguan Ji's petition.
translations.idiomatic: The sovereign lacked the clear judgment of Emperor Zhao of Han; the minister had a complaint like Shangguan Ji's.

sentences.zh: 嫌隙旣兆，釁故因之。

translations.literal: Suspicion and rift had already appeared; pretext for conflict followed upon it.
translations.idiomatic: Suspicion and breach had already shown themselves, and a cause for strife followed in their wake.

sentences.zh: 啟冢宰無君之心，成閔皇廢弒之禍，植之由也。

translations.literal: It awakened the grand minister's heart without a lord; it brought the calamity of Emperor Min's deposition and murder—Zhi was the cause.
translations.idiomatic: It exposed the grand minister's disloyal ambition, brought about the calamity of Emperor Xiaomin's deposition and murder—and Zhi was the source of it.

sentences.zh: 李遠旣闕義方之訓，又無先見之明，以是誅夷，非為不幸。

translations.literal: Li Yuan both lacked proper instruction in righteousness and lacked foresight; to be executed and exterminated for this was not misfortune.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuan had failed in proper family instruction and lacked foresight; that he was executed and his line destroyed was no undeserved fate.

sentences.zh: 全文以中華書局、一九七一年十一月版《周書》為本校。

translations.literal: The entire text uses the Zhonghua Shuju, November 1971 edition of the Book of Zhou, as the base for this collation.
translations.idiomatic: This text was collated against the Zhonghua Shuju edition of the 《Book of Zhou》 (November 1971).
